method: git grep across docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.control.yml, docker-compose.remote-dev.yml, docker-compose.exec.yml and services/**/*.py (excluding *_test.py/tests/) for PANTHEON_S3_*, PANTHEON_ARTIFACT_BUCKET, boto3, botocore, and an S3 client construction. Read-only; no secret values were read and no hosted system was mutated.

control_stack.note: client tag diverges from main_stack (pinned digest vs floating latest); both point at the same archived/unmaintained upstream per docs/reviews/2026-09-06-system-simplification/oss-findings.md line 34.

posture_only_readers_of_object_store_env.behavior: validate_persistence_posture() only checks that all four keys are non-empty strings when PANTHEON_PERSISTENCE_POSTURE/PANTHEON_ENV is stage/staging/prod. It never opens a network connection, never constructs an S3/GCS client, and never reads or writes an object.
posture_only_readers_of_object_store_env.docstring_confirmation: "The check is intentionally configuration-only ... It does not open database or object-store connections."

posture_only_readers_of_object_store_env.behavior: validate_source_search_posture() performs the same presence-only check for source-ingest/search staging/prod posture; no object I/O.

code_level_finding.conclusion: Every one of the 18 (main) / 12 (control) declared 'consumers' above only forwards or requires the four PANTHEON_S3_* env vars for a staging/prod posture gate. No service in services/**/*.py constructs a boto3/S3 client or performs an S3 GET/PUT against MinIO from application code. This proves no *source-code* consumer of the MinIO/S3 layer exists; it does not prove the hosted MinIO volume itself is empty (see existing_data_volumes below — hosted content was not inspected by this task).

real_object_store_consumers.kind: application service code (runs inside the BFF, on every environment)
real_object_store_consumers.behavior: prepare_inline_attachment()/store_inline_attachment() upload management-AI chat attachments to `gs://<bucket>/management-ai-attachments/<session>/<turn>/<id>-<filename>` via storage.Client().bucket(...).blob(...).upload_from_string(...); read() downloads the same object by its recorded storageUrl/objectName. When PANTHEON_MGMT_AI_ATTACH_BUCKET is unset it falls back to a local filesystem path (dev/local), never to MinIO/S3.
real_object_store_consumers.existing_isolated_proof: services/control-plane/bff/test_bff_mgmt_ai_persistence_2026_06_03.py::test_management_ai_attachment_store_uses_gcs_bucket_metadata (fake-bucket round trip of content, size, content-type, filename)
real_object_store_consumers.identity_semantics_required: opaque id + storageUrl/objectName path lookup only; no version/generation identity is read back by this consumer.
real_object_store_consumers.note: This is the only place in the repository where a running service writes and reads real object bytes through an external object-store API as part of its own request path. It already uses GCS, not MinIO/S3, and it is unrelated to the PANTHEON_S3_* variables above.

real_object_store_consumers.function: recovery source identity resolution (gcs_object branch, lines ~159-183)
real_object_store_consumers.kind: release-evidence / recovery-source-identity tooling (invoked out-of-band, not a running service)
real_object_store_consumers.backend: Google Cloud Storage, via `gcloud storage objects describe gs://<bucket>/<name> --format=json`
real_object_store_consumers.behavior: For a `recovery_source` of kind `gcs_object`, this reads the object's `bucket`, `name`, `generation`, `metageneration` (both automatically assigned by GCS on every write, per https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/metadata), and a `metadata.pantheon_sha256`/`metadata.sha256` field (custom object metadata that the uploader must set explicitly; GCS does not compute or attach it automatically), and fails closed (raises ValueError) if generation, metageneration, or a valid hex sha256 metadata value is missing.
real_object_store_consumers.identity_semantics_required: GCS-native object generation + metageneration (an immutable per-write version identity that GCS assigns automatically) plus a custom `pantheon_sha256`/`sha256` object-metadata field that is not automatic and must be written by whichever producer creates the object. This is a real reliance on GCS's built-in versioning-like identity plus a call-site metadata contract, not MinIO/S3 versioning, and it contradicts a 'no consumer needs versioning' claim about the object-store estate as a whole (it only holds for the MinIO/S3 layer, which is unused).
real_object_store_consumers.note: This identity contract is satisfied by GCS's own platform feature today (no extra bucket configuration is required to get generation/metageneration); it was not exercised against a real hosted bucket by this task (no gcloud credentials/network available in this read-only task), so its feasibility against an actual bucket remains unverified-in-isolation, not proven.

real_object_store_consumers.kind: deploy-time tooling (invoked out-of-band during VM deploy, not a running service)
real_object_store_consumers.backend: Google Cloud Storage JSON API via `curl` + a GCE metadata-service access token (no google-cloud-storage client library, no gcloud CLI)
real_object_store_consumers.behavior: POSTs a small probe object to `storage.googleapis.com/upload/storage/v1/b/<bucket>/o`, GETs it back with `alt=media`, compares bytes with `cmp -s`, then DELETEs the probe object — a real PUT/GET/DELETE round trip against the hosted `PANTHEON_MGMT_AI_ATTACH_BUCKET` bucket used by the deploy target environment.
real_object_store_consumers.identity_semantics_required: object PUT-by-name, GET-by-name, DELETE-by-name; no generation/metageneration read.
real_object_store_consumers.note: This is a real, already-existing PUT/GET/DELETE dependency on a hosted GCS bucket at deploy time; it directly contradicts any characterization of the object-store estate as having a single sole consumer. It is unrelated to MinIO/S3 and requires no MinIO/S3 replacement, since it already targets GCS.

retention_legal_hold_versioning_encrypti.finding: No service (MinIO-wired or GCS-wired) declares a bucket-level retention policy, legal-hold flag, bucket versioning flag, server-side-encryption key, or per-tenant bucket/prefix partition anywhere in docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.control.yml, or services/control-plane/bff/management_ai_store.py. The one attachment-store consumer partitions objects by session_id/turn_id path prefix only, inside a single shared bucket/prefix. Separately, `services/control-plane/bff/main.py`'s `bff_management_ai_attachment` handler (lines ~17354-17383) authorizes every attachment read at the application layer: it extracts the caller's tenant identity, resolves the attachment's owning session via `_management_ai_get_session_or_404(..., tenant_id=caller_tenant_id)`, and returns 404 before any object read if that session/tenant check fails.
retention_legal_hold_versioning_encrypti.implication: There is no bucket/prefix-level retention, legal-hold, versioning, or tenant-partition contract to preserve or migrate at the storage layer itself. There *is* an existing tenant-isolation contract, enforced above the storage layer at the BFF authorization boundary rather than by bucket/prefix structure; any storage cutover must keep routing every attachment read through that same session/tenant authorization check, not just preserve object bytes. `scripts/capture_canonical_telemetry_baseline.py`'s generation/metageneration/pantheon_sha256 identity requirement (see real_object_store_consumers above) is a second preserved-contract item: it is an immutability/integrity identity requirement, not a retention or tenant requirement.

existing_data_volumes.minio_data_docker_volume: declared (minio-data) in both docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.control.yml. No committed evidence of populated or empty hosted content was found or read; this task did not connect to a hosted MinIO instance, list its objects, or read its data. The volume's actual hosted content is unknown, not established as empty — the source-code finding above only shows that no application code path performs S3 I/O against it, which is a separate fact from what bytes, if any, already exist on a running hosted instance.
existing_data_volumes.gcs_bucket: PANTHEON_MGMT_AI_ATTACH_BUCKET is unset by default in both compose files (empty string), so the default posture for both stacks is the local-filesystem fallback, not a populated GCS bucket. This says nothing about whether a non-default hosted deployment has PANTHEON_MGMT_AI_ATTACH_BUCKET set and populated; that hosted state was not inspected by this task.

licensing_and_restore_ownership.minio_server: AGPLv3 community distribution; per docs/reviews/2026-09-06-system-simplification/oss-findings.md line 34 the upstream community repository was archived 2026-04-25 and is no longer maintained (source-only distribution going forward); the currently pinned digest and the two divergent `mc` client tags (RELEASE.2024-01-16T16-06-34Z vs latest) cannot be refreshed against a maintained upstream release.
licensing_and_restore_ownership.minio_bootstrap_tooling: scripts/bootstrap.sh also starts and depends on MinIO outside the two Compose files themselves: line 66 lists `minio` in INFRA_SERVICES and brings it up via `docker compose up -d`, and line 118 runs `docker compose run --rm minio-init` to create the bucket. Any downstream MinIO retirement (OSS-OBJECT-STORE-CUTOVER-001) must also update this script's INFRA_SERVICES list and its minio-init bootstrap step, not only the two docker-compose*.yml files.
licensing_and_restore_ownership.google_cloud_storage_client: Apache-2.0 licensed Python client (google-cloud-storage), backed by the managed Google Cloud Storage service under Google's standard GCP terms; restore/versioning/retention are GCS platform features configured on the bucket, not something Pantheon has to operate.
licensing_and_restore_ownership.restore_ownership_today: docs/deployment/vm-dev-staging-prod-management-plan.md §11.3 declares a general per-release restore-rehearsal and production-shaped restore-drill policy, and lists MinIO alongside Postgres/NATS among stateful backends covered by VM/data-disk backup, but neither it nor docs/deployment/evidence/ops-vm-env-phase0-20260825/service-inventory.md documents a MinIO-specific object-level restore/versioning procedure; restore ownership for MinIO objects today is the same generic VM-disk-snapshot policy as every other stateful backend, not a bucket-specific runbook.
